tasks.question: For a normally distributed outcome, test a mean increase of 0.2 units with SD 0.5 using a one-sided one-sample t test at alpha 0.05. What minimum integer number of participants achieves 80% power?

tasks.question: Plan a balanced repeated-measures ANOVA for the between-group main effect with two groups and 3 repeated measurements per participant. At every occasion, marginal SD is 2.5 and the group means are 51 and 49. Assume multivariate normal observations, compound symmetry with correlation 0.5, no missing data and no group-by-time interaction. For the group effect use the subject-level average with a pooled t test (equivalently the between-group F test), alpha 0.05 two-sided. What minimum integer participants per group achieves 80% power?

tasks.question: Plan a one-group repeated-measures ANOVA with 3 time points, multivariate normal data, compound symmetry correlation 0.5, and no missing data. For the within-time omnibus effect use the univariate F test with sphericity epsilon 1. The G*Power population effect is partial eta-squared 0.08 before the correlation adjustment (f-squared = eta-squared/(1-eta-squared)). At alpha 0.05, what minimum total integer sample size achieves 90% power?

tasks.question: Use the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation in Field Trials of Health Interventions Chapter 5, Section 6.1, including its additive one-cluster correction. Treatment/control rates are 0.005/0.010 per child-week, exposure is 2500 child-weeks per cluster, and the between-cluster coefficient of variation is 0.25. For 90% power, two-sided alpha 0.05 and equal allocation, calculate clusters per arm, rounding upward.

tasks.question: Calculate the minimum total development sample size for a binary clinical prediction model using the Riley criteria as implemented by pmsampsize 1.1.3. There are 24 candidate predictor parameters (excluding intercept), prevalence 0.174 and anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared 0.288. Use shrinkage 0.90 and the package default precision criteria; do not use events-per-variable rules. Precision uses 95% confidence and maximum absolute apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared difference 0.05 (Nagelkerke scale for binary/survival). Target average outcome-risk absolute margin of error 0.05; for survival verify this precision at the returned package sample size.
tasks.exposure_status: Previously developer-exposed; not a held-out evaluation question

provenance.locator: Manual pp.5, binary example; Riley et al., Statistics in Medicine, doi:10.1002/sim.7992

tasks.question: For a binary clinical outcome, reproduce the Verma Chapter 7 Illustration 7.2 large-sample logistic coefficient-test planning convention: G*Power 3.1.9.2 Demidenko (2007) WITH variance correction, not Hsieh or an enumeration likelihood-ratio test. Let event probability at X=0 be 0.10 and at X=1 be 0.30; X follows standard normal X, mean 0 and SD 1. R-squared of X explained by other predictors is 0.1. Use alpha 0.05, one-sided test, target power 0.85, no attrition. Determine the smallest integer total participants and recompute approximate power at that N and N - 1. This is an approximation for detecting a predictor coefficient, not sizing overall prediction-model development or guaranteeing finite-sample power.

tasks.question: For a binary clinical outcome, reproduce the Verma Chapter 7 Illustration 7.3 large-sample logistic coefficient-test planning convention: G*Power 3.1.9.2 Demidenko (2007) WITH variance correction, not Hsieh or an enumeration likelihood-ratio test.
